newsitem.title: CANADA: Flight attendants strike Air Canada unit.
newsitem.headline: Flight attendants strike Air Canada unit.

text.p: About 140 flight attendants at Air Canada's Air Ontario unit went on strike Sunday night, Air Ontario and union officials said on Monday.

Air Ontario president Stephen Smith said the airline is using replacement workers and business is running as usual. But union officials said flights from Toronto were still facing more than one hour delays on Monday.

Several flights were cancelled or delayed on Sunday night when the attendants walked off the job at 1930 EST/0030 GMT. Locals 4046 and 4019 of the airline division of the Canadian Union of Public Employees are involved.
"Last night, until we ironed out some wrinkles, we had a couple of flights cancelled but it's business as usual today," Smith said in a telephone interview.
Air Ontario runs about 200 flights per day around Ontario and to the United States, Quebec and Manitoba.
Attendants are pressing for higher wages, improved working conditions and shorter shifts, Denise Hill, president of the airline division of the Canadian Union of Public Employees said.
Flight attendants have been without a contract since August 31.
She said attendants are now expected to work 15 hours per shift and cover eight to nine landings. The union is asking that to be shortened to 14 hours and seven landings.
Air Canada is facing more strife in its regional airline division in the coming days. Pilots at its regional airlines are planning to walk out on January 10.

The Canadian Air Line Pilots Association said 900 pilots for regional airlines Air Ontario, AirBC, Air Alliance and Air Nova will go on strike if they do not get a settlement. Smith said Air Ontario has a "contingency plan" if there is a pilot strike, but he declined to give details.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
